title: Temple of Isis in Philae
visualBrief: Specific standing Isis complex on Agilkia: two differently aligned battered twin pylons/real central passages and smaller first-tower door, cavetto cornices/flagstaff slots, original simplified shallow figure/register vocabulary, mapped rear sanctuary with both open roof courts, west birth-house-like range and east court portico with flared plant-capital columns, plus both mapped long forecourt colonnades. Native open courts/forecourt retained. No island slab, copied deity/story/hieroglyph atlas, complete hidden ritual interior or neighboring Trajan kiosk/independent monuments.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Retained exact-QID temple-siteway93872388/Q1503673, named standard PMTiles Philae Temple point35184465961220 and five mapped controls35184572861120,35185194956229,35185194956230,35185198368745,52776560831061 correlate the occupied Isis structures. Site boundary is not itself a building footprint. Anchor32.88423049,24.025280187; heading0. First pylon/west and east court ranges use internal+.287rad cross-axis; second pylon/rear sanctuary cross-axis about+.544rad, correctly distinct. Entrance south/local+z. Actual mapped outlines/roof holes establish extent, but interior allocations, exact columns, heights and ornament approximate. All other independent monuments/buildings remain native.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Ordinary-picture/map visualization estimates: first pylon36.1m wide/towers18.5m high, second27.4m wide/towers13.5m, central passages3.7x6m and3.3x5.5m. West court range around9.6x22.7m and8m high, east range7.2x20.5m and7m high. Rear sanctuary8.7m/9.4m roof/cornice with both mapped holes open; columns roughly6-8m. Forecourt west32 and east17 picture-led column stations, west court12 and east court7, two roof courts4 each. Bay/capital/relief inventories and absolute levels are approximations, not surveys.
